executiveSummary: According to these articles, UEFA has filed legal requests in US federal courts to obtain testimony and documents from FIFA entities in Florida and a New York investment fund. These materials are intended for use in a planned criminal complaint in Switzerland against FIFA President Gianni Infantino. The complaint alleges criminal mismanagement related to a now-abandoned plan to transfer World Cup commercial rights into a new subsidiary called FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE).

timeline.dateSource: Infantino was forced to scrap the plan on Aug. 1
timeline.description: Infantino scrapped the World Cup private investment plan.

timeline.dateSource: UEFA, which issued a blistering statement saying it had lost confidence in Infantino's leadership at FIFA, first threatened to take legal action on Aug. 3
timeline.description: UEFA threatened to take legal action against FIFA over the FFE plan.

timeline.dateSource: UEFA said it filed a request in the southern Florida district court for authorization of discovery 'in a foreign proceeding' against FIFA
timeline.description: UEFA filed a request in a US federal court to obtain evidence for the Swiss criminal complaint.

significance.reasoning: This story involves a direct challenge to the leadership of FIFA, the world's governing body for football, by its largest regional confederation, UEFA. The move to a criminal complaint in Switzerland, rather than a civil suit, is a significant escalation. The involvement of US courts to compel evidence further internationalizes the conflict. The reporting describes a potential major financial and governance crisis at the heart of global sport.

entities.name: UEFA
entities.role: The European football governing body. It is the accuser, having filed court requests to obtain evidence and is preparing a criminal complaint in Switzerland against Infantino.

entities.name: Gianni Infantino
entities.role: The President of FIFA. He is the target of the planned criminal complaint, accused of developing a secret plan to profit from World Cup commercial rights.

entities.name: FIFA
entities.role: The international governing body of football. Its President is Infantino. Specific entities named in the discovery requests are FIFA (AMERICAS), Inc. and FWC2026 US, Inc.

entities.name: FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE)
entities.role: A proposed new subsidiary mentioned in the reporting. The plan to transfer World Cup commercial rights into this entity was the subject of the criminal complaint.

entities.name: Joshua Kushner
entities.role: The younger brother of Jared Kushner. He is mentioned as a potential investor in the FFE plan and is the founder of Thrive Capital Management.

entities.name: Thrive Capital Management
entities.role: A New York investment fund founded by Joshua Kushner. UEFA filed a separate request in a Manhattan court to obtain evidence from this fund.

sources.bias: The core legal claims are reported by the AFP news agency and corroborated by CBS News, a major international broadcaster. The details of the court filings and the specific allegations are directly sourced from the legal documents themselves, which provides a high level of reliability for the factual reporting.

factualBasis: Infantino scrapped the World Cup private investment plan.
UEFA threatened to take legal action against FIFA over the FFE plan.
UEFA filed a request in a US federal court to obtain evidence for the Swiss criminal complaint.
informationGaps: There is no reporting from FIFA, Gianni Infantino, or Thrive Capital Management providing their response or perspective to the allegations.
The articles do not provide the specific details of the 'criminal mismanagement' under Article 158 of the Swiss Criminal Code.
The reporting does not mention the involvement or reaction of other FIFA member associations or confederations beyond UEFA.
The articles do not state the outcome of the court filings or whether the discovery requests have been granted.
